rules: Manual aiBridge.bat launch prints local status and usage guidance instead of silently waiting on stdin.
MCP / AI clients must launch aiBridgeServer.bat or aiBridge.bat --stdio.
No arbitrary shell command tool.
No absolute paths and no parent traversal in file tools.
Mutating commands require an explicit process-level write flag.
Suite command execution delegates to SuiteRegistry through tools/scripts/takesome.py suite --run when present.
The bridge is an operator/Suite entry layer, not an engine runtime dependency.
OpenAI API keys are cached only under .takesome/secrets/openai_api_key.local, which is local generated state.
OPENAI_API_KEY from the process environment overrides the cached key.
Silent stdio server mode never asks interactive questions because it must preserve the MCP JSON-RPC stream.
HTTP mode is started with aiBridge.bat http and exposes MCP-compatible JSON-RPC through POST /mcp.
stdio mode remains silent and is started with aiBridge.bat stdio or aiBridgeServer.bat.
dataSetDirectory archives are scanned by explicit dataset tools; extracted directory mirrors are preferred after materialization.
Continuous work is an observe/analyze/patch/build loop driven by the AI client; the bridge stays alive, prints status and logs every request.
Direct write_text, patch_text and apply_changed_files_zip require NORTHSTAR_AI_BRIDGE_WRITE=1 and create backups under .takesome/ai-bridge/patch-backups.
Unlisted SuiteRegistry actions may be executed only in write mode through takesome.py suite --run <action_id>; no arbitrary shell is exposed.
Operator notes/state/cache/scratch are generated local state and must never contain secrets.
serverBridge.bat should prefer the declared Cloudflare named tunnel before creating a quick trycloudflare.com tunnel.
Cloudflare tunnel transport is a deployment/provider concern; bridge HTTP origin remains local at 127.0.0.1:8765.
QUIC must remain available as a fallback transport instead of being removed from the tunnel policy.
serverBridge.bat owns the public tunnel and must keep the local 127.0.0.1:8765 MCP origin alive while the tunnel is running.
If an already-running local origin is adopted at startup and later disappears, the supervisor starts its own origin process instead of leaving Cloudflare with a refused origin port.
Cloudflare transport fallback is supervisor-level: QUIC is tried first for ChatGPT connector compatibility, then auto/HTTP2 only if tunnel startup fails.
Project config transport policy has priority over stale .takesome local tunnel state; environment variables remain the only higher-priority override.
Cloudflare quick route mode must not prompt for stable hostname setup; it allocates a fresh trycloudflare.com endpoint directly.
The connector endpoint is printed only after the quick route public /health check verifies, otherwise supervisor retries fallback transports.
A single dot is not a valid stable hostname and must be treated as quick-route fallback, not passed to cloudflared tunnel route dns.
Cloudflare quick route startup must temporarily hide default %USERPROFILE%/.cloudflared/config.yml or config.yaml so TryCloudflare does not inherit named-tunnel credentials and produce Error 1033.
The quick route endpoint is usable only after public /health verifies through the generated trycloudflare.com URL; allocated URL alone is not enough.
TryCloudflare quick tunnels must run in an isolated cloudflared home and must not inherit named tunnel credentials from the operator profile.
Do not restore %USERPROFILE%/.cloudflared/config.yml while the quick tunnel cloudflared process is still alive; restore it only after the process stops.
dataSetDirectory zip archives are ingest-only transport objects: materialize into extracted/ with manifest, then delete the .zip source.
Operator memory is generated state with retention hygiene: old task/knowledge/note/cache overflow is pruned while current state is refreshed into typed operator state.
OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable has priority over local cache.
If a Suite/OpenAI request requires a key and none is available, interactive console mode prompts once and caches the key under .takesome.
MCP stdio mode never prompts on stdin/stdout; it returns openai_key_missing and asks the operator to run aiBridge.bat --openai-login.
The key is never printed in full and is never passed through command-line arguments.

http.console: colored status, heartbeat and per-request logs

notes: serverBridge.bat is configured for Cloudflare quick route mode: it asks Cloudflare for a fresh trycloudflare.com public route at startup instead of using the .ru hostname.
Quick route mode skips interactive named tunnel setup even when serverBridge.bat passes --setup-named.
Use the printed https://*.trycloudflare.com/mcp endpoint in ChatGPT connector creation only after the supervisor logs that public health verified.
QUIC is tried first for ChatGPT connector compatibility; auto/http2 remain startup fallbacks.
The previous named .ru route is preserved under named_fallback and can be restored by changing route_mode back to named.
The supervisor health-checks http://127.0.0.1:8765/health while the tunnel is running and restarts the local origin if it disappears.

TryCloudflare quick tunnels are started with the default Cloudflare config files temporarily hidden, because cloudflared cannot reliably run quick tunnels when ~/.cloudflared/config.yml or config.yaml is present.

If the browser shows Cloudflare Error 1033 on a quick route, it usually means the generated hostname has no healthy cloudflared connector; restart serverBridge.bat and use only the endpoint printed after public health verification.

Quick tunnel launch uses an isolated subprocess HOME/USERPROFILE under .takesome/ai-bridge/cloudflared-quick-home so account-bound named tunnel config/credentials cannot leak into trycloudflare startup.
Default Cloudflare config files remain hidden for the whole lifetime of the quick tunnel process and are restored only when serverBridge stops or retries a fallback transport.
